C3075.definition: An array is one of the things that a for each loop can be used for, together with collections of homogeneous data types.

C3076.name: collection
C3076.definition: A collection is a collection of homogeneous data types that a foreach loop can work with directly instead of dealing with individual data types.

C3077.name: homogeneous data type
C3077.definition: A homogeneous data type is a data type in an array or collection that a foreach loop can work with directly.

C3078.name: transform property
C3078.definition: The transform property is a property attached to every game object in a scene that stores the object's position, rotation, and scale and can be modified programmatically through a script.

C3079.name: transform.Translate
C3079.definition: Transform.Translate is used in a script, such as in a game object's update function, to modify the object's transform property so the object behaves as desired.

C3080.name: local scale
C3080.definition: Local scale is a set of values used in a script to modify the scale stored in a game object's transform, so the object can behave as desired.

C3081.name: coroutine
C3081.definition: A coroutine is a method that allows a developer to spread tasks across several frames by pausing execution, returning control, and continuing where it left off on the following frame; it does not create threads and its operations still execute on the main thread.

C3082.name: thread
C3082.definition: A thread is an execution unit, such as the main thread or an individual thread, and it is not a coroutine.

C3083.name: main thread
C3083.definition: Main thread is the thread on which synchronous operations within a coroutine execute.

C3084.name: synchronous operation
C3084.definition: Synchronous operation is an operation that, within a coroutine, executes on the main thread.

C3085.name: opacity
C3085.definition: Opacity is a value of an object that, when reduced over a sequence of frames, makes a gradual fade visible.

C3086.name: opacity fade
C3086.definition: Opacity fade is a gradual reduction of an object's alpha or opacity over a sequence of frames so that intermediate values are rendered and visible.

C3087.name: InvokeRepeating
C3087.definition: InvokeRepeating is a method that takes a function name and two times in seconds, invoking the function after the initial delay and then repeatedly at the repeat interval.

C3088.name: initial delay
C3088.definition: Initial delay is a time value, in seconds, that specifies how long to wait before a repeatedly invoked method first starts.

C3089.name: interval
C3089.definition: An interval is a specified time in seconds that sets how often a method is repeatedly invoked after an initial delay.

C3090.name: input support
C3090.definition: Input support is imported software development kit input support that may be needed for device-specific inputs and extends inbuilt support.

C3091.name: build
C3091.definition: Build is the process in the Unity development environment that creates a package for a selected platform from the selected scenes, so the system can be published or deployed.

C3092.name: Build Settings window
C3092.definition: The Build Settings window is a Unity editor window that contains the settings and options for publishing a built system, including the scenes in the build, the selected platform, and the Build or Build and Run button that begins the build process.

C3093.name: File Build Settings
C3093.definition: File Build Settings is the Unity editor path used to reach the Build Settings window, which contains all settings and options to publish or deploy a build.

C3094.name: Scenes in Build panel
C3094.definition: Scenes in Build panel is a panel in the Build Settings window of the Unity development environment's editor that manages which scenes are included in a build.

C3095.name: Build button
C3095.definition: The Build button is a button in the Unity editor's Build Settings window that begins the build process.

C3096.name: Build and Run button
C3096.definition: The Build and Run button is a button in the Unity development environment's editor that begins the build process.

C3097.name: Unity layered architecture
C3097.definition: Unity layered architecture is a layered architecture in which the application is the top layer and a software development kit (SDK) layer above the Unity layer is treated as part of the installed Unity package.

C3098.name: software development kit layer
C3098.definition: A software development kit layer is a layer in a Unity layered architecture, positioned on top of the Unity layer, that is treated as part of the installed Unity package whose application programming interfaces are used.

C3099.name: Unity layer
C3099.definition: A Unity layer is a layer in the Unity layered architecture, positioned below the software development kit (SDK) layer.

C3100.name: object detection
C3100.definition: Object detection is an object recognition or computer vision operation.

C3101.name: ios
C3101.definition: Ios is a platform supported by the cross-platform Vuforia software development kit.

C3102.name: license
C3102.definition: A license is required to use Vuforia and is added to a Unity project from a Vuforia account.

C3103.name: vuforia engine
C3103.definition: Vuforia engine is used in marker-based augmented reality to recognize images or markers from a database and display a 3D model in place of the marker.

C3104.name: vuforia configuration
C3104.definition: Vuforia configuration is a configuration that requires a Vuforia account and license, with the license added to the Unity project from that account.

C3105.name: vuforia account
C3105.definition: A vuforia account is an account required for Vuforia configuration, from which a license is added to a Unity project.

C3106.name: vuforia setup
C3106.definition: Vuforia setup is the process in which a new database is created on the Vuforia website, images or markers to be tracked are added to that database, and the downloaded database package file is imported into the project so the Vuforia engine can recognize them.

C3107.name: database
C3107.definition: A database is a Vuforia file containing images or markers to be tracked, imported into a project for recognition.

C3108.name: main camera
C3108.definition: The main camera is a camera in a Unity sample scene that is removed when a Vuforia augmented reality camera is selected.

C3109.name: augmented reality camera
C3109.definition: Augmented reality camera is a Unity camera used in a sample scene together with an image target.

C3110.name: image target
C3110.definition: An image target is a Vuforia AR component to which a target image and a 3D model are assigned, and to which a behavior script can be attached.

C3111.name: image target behavior script
C3111.definition: An image target behavior script is a script that is attached to or used to modify the behavior of a Vuforia image target and performs the operations after the Vuforia engine recognizes the marker.

C3112.name: unity player settings
C3112.definition: Unity player settings are application-specific settings configured under Edit > Project Settings > Player > Other, where the scripting backend, minimum API level, and ARM version are set.

C3113.name: advanced risc machines
C3113.definition: Advanced RISC Machines (ARM) is a Unity player setting that is checked or unchecked when configuring a sample project.

C3114.name: il2cpp scripting backend
C3114.definition: Il2cpp scripting backend is a Unity player setting used to configure a sample project.

C3115.name: api level
C3115.definition: API level is a Unity player setting that is configured to be greater than 7 in the sample project.

C3116.name: universal serial bus
C3116.definition: Universal serial bus (USB) is a cable used to connect an Android device that has USB debugging enabled.

C3117.name: usb debugging
C3117.definition: USB debugging is enabled on an Android device connected through a USB cable when an Android package is built and run directly on that device.

C3118.name: android package
C3118.definition: An android package (APK) is a file created when building for the Android platform that can be deployed directly to an Android device or transferred and installed separately.

C3119.name: image recognition
C3119.definition: Image recognition is a functionality that a software development kit can add to a Unity development environment.

C3120.name: edge computing
C3120.definition: Edge computing is a computing concept that is relevant for scalable and affordable extended reality systems and for addressing resource optimization concerns.

C3121.name: robotics
C3121.definition: Robotics is a technology relevant to extended reality applications.

C3122.name: blockchain
C3122.definition: Blockchain is a relevant technology for extended reality applications.
